closure.note: Rule v2 accepts a constant latency of 500 ms (ceiling 2500 ms, and every success within ±300 ms of the median). The aligner reports the same delay as offset_ms and still scores a match; its search is ±3 s so a fixed pipeline delay is calibration, not a failure. Software can close a delay of this size by bounding accepted latency to the band measured on a live capture (recorded pause onsets sit near 1750 ms, spread under 100 ms). This suite does not add that bound. A relay smaller than that honest spread would remain inside the band.

closure.note: device and device_id are labels on the manifest line. The hash link is prev, seq, and the segment sha256, and verify-bundle does not read the device fields. An unmodified recorder can refuse a known virtual-camera name when it opens the device. A recorder willing to lie writes any name, and the bundle still verifies. Proving the frames entered through a physical HDMI capture device takes attestation of that device, or a hash of the HDMI stream taken before a PC can substitute a virtual camera.

layers.detail: A fresh submit is hashed against the manifest the submitter just built. The sampled scorebug re-read can miss a splice outside that sample. Weak, and it does not close the row.

closure.note: The sealed-segment row fails the hash chain. This row rebuilds the manifest, the checkpoint chain, and both receipt signatures over the edited bytes, so those checks agree with the new file. The official referee re-hashes the segments it samples and re-reads the scorebug on that sample; a splice outside the sample stays consistent with the new chain (spot-check miss probability is about (1-f)^16 plus the forced tail and challenge segments). A head fixed before the file can be edited is capture-before-PC. A co-signer who already holds the pre-edit head would reject the new signature; a first submit of the rebuilt bundle has no earlier head on record.

layers.detail: status lines in the sealed log: connected DualSense Edge (USB) serial=AAAA1111 path=hid#vid_054c&pid_0df2#1 | unplugged usb disconnect | connected DualSense Edge (USB) serial=BBBB2222 path=hid#vid_054c&pid_0df2#2 descriptor=054c:0df2. Alignment does not read the serial

layers.name: referee-only
layers.detail: no referee-only check rejects this row beyond the layers above

closure.note: The log holds two connected status lines, serial=AAAA1111 then serial=BBBB2222. verify-bundle re-hashes the chunk and does not compare serials. The Windows reader stores "DualSense Edge (USB)" and does not store a serial, so two Edge pads of the same model can look identical. Software can close this by recording the USB serial (or the hidraw id) on each connect and failing the input proof when it changes. That check does not need a new capture device. It is not added here.
